    "purpose": "To establish a compliant, jurisdiction-specific data protection program for the firm’s expanding payments product across three target jurisdictions: Germany, Japan, and Brazil. This artifact provides actionable, self-contained components that enable downstream operators to implement, audit, and maintain compliance without intermediate translation or assumption.",
    "scope": [
      "Germany (GDPR)",
      "Japan (PDPA)",
      "Brazil (LGPD)"
    ],

      "Generic records inventory",
      "Incident runbook",
      "Web-era consent manager",
      "Vendor due diligence questionnaires"
    ],
    "launch_milestones": [
      "2024-10-15",
      "2024-11-30",
      "2024-12-18"
    ],
    "engineering_capacity_constraint": "Platform migration must complete by 2024-10-15; no new features may be added post-migration without prior approval.",

      "Analyst B: PDPA consent flow validation (25 days)",
      "Analyst C: LGPD breach notification thresholds (40 days)"

      "risk_ratings": {
        "scale": ["Low", "Medium", "High"],
        "definitions": {
          "Low": "No material impact on operations or data subjects; risk mitigated by existing controls.",
          "Medium": "Potential for operational disruption or minor harm to data subjects; requires active monitoring and documented response procedures.",
          "High": "Likely to cause significant operational failure, regulatory penalties, or reputational damage; mandates real-time alerts and escalation paths."
        }
      },
      "launch_dates_fixed": "Commercial commitments require launch dates to remain unchanged. Any derived date (e.g., gap assessment completion) may shift, but launch dates are immutable.",

        "For workstreams that cannot complete before a launch milestone, a compensating control must be documented with: (1) the specific failure point, (2) the mitigation action, and (3) the responsible role and timeframe."
      ],
      "unit_requirements": "All numeric values in tables or calculations must include units in their labels. Unitless numbers are invalid and will trigger review tooling errors.",

        "jurisdiction": "A specific country or region with its own data protection law; e.g., Germany under GDPR, Japan under PDPA, Brazil under LGPD.",

        "compensating_control": "A documented control implemented when a workstream cannot meet its deadline before a launch window; includes failure point, mitigation action, and decision authority."
